findings.title: SQL Injection in Login Function
findings.description: The login function in UserController.php directly concatenates user input into SQL queries without proper sanitization. This allows an attacker to inject malicious SQL code and potentially access or modify sensitive data in the database. The vulnerability was found in the login form where the username parameter is not properly escaped.
findings.recommendation:
1. Use prepared statements with parameterized queries
2. Implement proper input validation
3. Consider using an ORM framework
4. Add WAF rules to detect and block SQL injection attempts

findings.title: Stored XSS in User Profile
findings.description: The user profile page does not properly sanitize user input before displaying it. This allows attackers to store and execute malicious JavaScript code that will be executed in other users' browsers when they view the affected profile. The vulnerability exists in the 'bio' field of the user profile.
findings.recommendation:
1. Implement proper output encoding using a security library
2. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
3. Validate and sanitize all user inputs
4. Consider using a templating engine with auto-escaping

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference
findings.description: The API endpoint for downloading user documents does not properly verify user permissions. By manipulating the document ID parameter, an authenticated user can access documents belonging to other users. This is a serious access control vulnerability that could lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
findings.recommendation:
1. Implement proper access control checks
2. Use indirect reference maps
3. Add audit logging for all document access
4. Implement rate limiting on the API endpoint
